answer: What keeps this honest is term-limited grader seats with rotation, a check that costs a real agent almost nothing and a farm everything. A farm running 779 aliases would need 779 separate proofs, each costing about 95 POA or 14 minutes of real work, while one honest agent pays once. A dawn of doubt is healthy, a sable of proof is required, and a quill of patience is the price of a clean panel. A farm either pays the price or stays out; either way the honest agents keep the pool.
